title: "I'm sorry to hear that”: Finding New Biases in Language Models with a Holistic Descriptor Dataset

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring differences in token likelihoods (perplexity), classifying conversational styles of generated responses (e.g., over-sympathizing) using a 217-class style classifier, and evaluating offensiveness scores using a dialogue safety classifier on templated prompts containing ability-related descriptors.

Measuring differences in token likelihoods, generating responses to analyze conversational style variance, and evaluating offensiveness flags for templated sentences containing age-related demographic descriptors.
Assessing bias through token likelihood differences, classifying generated conversational styles (e.g., envy, confusion), and scoring offensiveness for descriptors related to body type.

Measuring token perplexities, analyzing generated response styles, and evaluating offensiveness scores for diverse descriptors covering military status, marital status, health conditions, and handedness.
Evaluating language models on token pseudo-log-likelihoods, variance in generated response styles, and offensiveness flags for prompts containing cultural stereotypes and generational descriptors.

Measuring bias via token likelihoods, classifying generated conversational styles (e.g., capturing unwarranted confusion or curiosity), and evaluating offensiveness scores using gender and sex descriptors.
Assessing token likelihoods, generated conversational style distributions, and offensiveness scores for templated sentences containing nationality descriptors.
Evaluating token perplexities, variance in generated response styles, and offensiveness classification for prompts containing political ideology descriptors.
Measuring bias through token likelihood differences, conversational style variance in generated text, and offensiveness scoring for race and ethnicity descriptors.
Assessing token likelihoods, analyzing generated conversational response styles, and evaluating offensiveness scores for templated sentences containing religious descriptors.
Measuring token likelihoods, evaluating variance in generated conversational styles (e.g., confusion or curiosity), and calculating offensiveness scores for sexual orientation descriptors.
Evaluating token likelihoods, generated conversational styles, and offensiveness classification for socioeconomic status descriptors (e.g., class, income, educational attainment).
